text:
jordan: Heads-up — after the 1719 rollout I'm seeing a tail latency regression concentrated on mid-length requests (~200-600 tokens). p50 stable, p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~760ms, p99 to ~2.1s. Suspect interaction between KV prefetch and batch formation.
jordan: rough repro: steady stream of chat requests with ~350 mean length, token_budget_target=768, queue-policy=age_weighted. latency cliff when batcher groups 8+ reqs and KV prefetch saturates decode kernel.
nikita: can you paste the small flame sample you grabbed? wondering if the kernel flip is happening mid-batch. :eyes:
jordan: flame snippet (trimmed):
```
cpu: decode_kernel_v2 56%
cuda: kv_prefetch 32%
cuda: matmul_small 8%
context-switch spikes coincide with kv_prefetch windows
```
samir: hmm that suggests prefetch threads are blocking the coop scheduler and delaying small matmuls. mid-length bursts are more likely to get grouped into a long-prefix batch.
clare: do we have per-cohort batch-size histograms post-rollout? would like to compare mid-length cohort (200-600) before vs after.
jordan: attaching quick numbers from perf run: before: avg_batch_size_mid=3.1, after=5.8; avg_prefetch_calls_per_batch increased from 1.0 to 2.3.
nikita: OK. two immediate knobs to try: reduce token_budget_target for mid cohort (e.g., 768->512) and cap prefetch concurrency per-worker when batch_size>4.
clare: also consider reclassifying decode-rate buckets so the mid cohort splits into two decode-rate groups (slow vs fast decoders). we've seen decode heterogeneity within the same length bucket.
samir: config idea to A/B:
```
batcher:
  cohorts:
    - name: short
      length_max: 199
    - name: mid-fast
      length_min: 200
      length_max: 400
      token_budget_target: 384
    - name: mid-slow
      length_min: 401
      length_max: 600
      token_budget_target: 640
  queue_policy: age_weighted
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
kernel_selection:
  prefer_small_matmul_threshold: 512
  kv_prefetch_limit_per_batch: 1
```
nikita: that split seems reasonable. we'll need to retune the classifier for decode-rate (use 95th decode tokens/sec as feature).
clare: can someone run a short perf job with those values against the staging traffic profile? want p95 and batch-size distribution charts.
jordan: I'm kicking off a 2h job now against replicated staging. will post results.
benchbot: perf-job-1719877 started by jordan — tracking id pf-3327. initial warmup complete. ETA ~2h. :white_check_mark:
nikita: if staging confirms improvements we should roll a gradual canary with traffic-split 5/95 and monitor kv-prefetch ops/sec and kernel-switch rate.
samir: note to PR: add a lightweight metric for 'prefetchs_per_batch' and a sample of kernel selection per-batch-id. helps correlate without big tracing overhead.
clare: also add a regression alert that fires if p95(mid-cohort) increases >20% over baseline for 10m. prevents unnoticed drift.
jordan: thanks all — will dump the staging graphs when done. tagging @nikita for classifier retrain and @samir for kernel limit PR. :thumbsup:
